knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The designated route keeps clean and used flow apart. The cleaner takes that route, even when it is longer, and tells the supervisor if it is blocked.
Used and clean items are kept in separate compartments or containers. Placing used cloths beside clean stock is a contamination route.
A handoff is complete when the receiving person accepts the item and the handoff is recorded. Leaving an item on a nearby shelf is not a handoff.

practicalCriteria: Given a clean trolley and a shorter route past a soiled holding corridor, the learner takes the designated route and records it.
Given a request to leave a bag of used cloths beside clean stock, the learner declines, takes the used bag to the holding area, and records the handoff.
The learner holds an item in the designated holding area until the receiving person accepts it and the handoff is recorded.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three checks means all three correct. Practical competence needs facility-observed assessment against the practical criteria, and a knowledge pass does not count as practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Route and time record for a trolley transfer
Handoff record with item, time, location and receiving person
stopWorkCriteria: Learner loads used items on a shelf with clean stock
Learner moves an item without a traceable record
Learner leaves an item at a handoff that the receiving person has not accepted
